topic: The Windmill Problem (Computational Geometry & Sweep-Line Algorithm)
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Computer Science or Mathematics

outline.topic: The Windmill Problem (Computational Geometry & Sweep-Line Algorithm)
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Computer Science or Mathematics

sections.title: Introduction & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Define the Windmill problem: Given a set of points in a plane, imagine a line anchored at one point rotating like a windmill blade. The goal is to track the order of points the line hits as it rotates 360 degrees.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm sweeping across a field of stars; every time it 'strikes' a star, it records the event.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Angular Sorting (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of angular sweep. Explain how to represent point positions using polar coordinates relative to the pivot. Emphasize that the 'event' occurs when the angle of another point aligns with the current rotation angle.
sections.example: A compass needle rotating; points are 'ticked off' the list based on their angle relative to the North pole (the vertical axis).

sections.title: The Core Mechanism: The Swap Operation (1:45-3:15)
sections.content: Explain the state transition. When the line hits a point, the line 'pivot' moves to that point. Mathematically, this is a swap of the line's anchor point. We maintain a sorted list of points by angle and update the list incrementally to keep the next collision detection efficient.
sections.example: Two squirrels jumping over each other in a line; once they swap positions, the order of the 'queue' changes, and we recalculate the next target.

sections.title: Visualizing the Event Queue (3:15-4:15)
sections.content: Show a graphical representation where a line sweeps clockwise. As it hits points, highlights show the 'event queue' updating. Highlight the time complexity O(N^2 log N) vs O(N^2) based on sorted updates.
sections.example: An animation of a searchlight hitting points. Each hit triggers a 'ding' sound, and the line instantly re-orients its pivot to the point just struck.

sections.title: Summary & Complexity Analysis (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Recap the logic: Pivot selection + Angular sorting + Incremental updates. Conclude why this is essential for convex hull algorithms and computational geometry.
sections.example: Summarize the 'Windmill' as a fundamental building block for 'Dualization' in geometry, transforming complex spatial relationships into a simple sequence of events.

storyboard.title: Introduction & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Imagine a rotating line anchored at a point.
It sweeps like a windmill blade across points.
We track the order of points hit sequentially.
Every strike records a unique event in space.
This reveals spatial relationships between all points.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Angular Sorting (0:45-1:45)
lecture_lines: Points are represented using polar coordinates.
Events occur when angles align with rotation.
We sort points angularly relative to the pivot.

storyboard.title: The Core Mechanism: The Swap Operation (1:45-3:15)
lecture_lines: Hitting a point changes the line's pivot.
This is mathematically a swap of anchor points.
We incrementally update the sorted angular list.
Efficient updates keep collision detection fast.
The mechanism continuously repeats for every hit.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Event Queue (3:15-4:15)
lecture_lines: A line sweeps clockwise hitting points.
Hits trigger updates to our event queue.
This optimization achieves high-performance computational geometry.
Visualizing highlights the algorithm's rapid progression.
Complex hits map to a simple sequence.

storyboard.title: Summary & Complexity Analysis (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: The windmill combines sorting and incremental updates.
It builds a foundational geometric event sequence.
Essential for advanced algorithms like convex hulls.
